source.title: Stories of Ancient Stones: A Living Tradition of Indigenous People (Mundas) in Jharkhand, India

exact_locators.locator: publisher PDF, printed p. 12 / PDF page index 9, Research Design and Site Selection
exact_locators.supported_metadata: Qualitative ethnographic and participatory design; multiple Munda villages in Ranchi are described as the study setting.

exact_locators.locator: publisher PDF, printed pp. 12-13 / PDF page indexes 9-10, Participant Selection and Table 1
exact_locators.supported_metadata: The paper reports participants aged 18-70 from rural Ranchi, snowball recruitment, and 15 Munda participants.
exact_locators.restriction: Do not ingest participant-level rows, pseudonym-linked attributes or statements as reusable cultural evidence without separate secondary-use/cultural-access justification.

exact_locators.locator: publisher PDF, printed pp. 13-14 / PDF page indexes 10-11, Data Collection and Data Analysis
exact_locators.supported_metadata: The paper reports participant observation, informal/semi-structured interviews, oral narratives, participatory methods, focus groups/interviews with women, and thematic/narrative analysis.

exact_locators.locator: publisher PDF, printed p. 14 / PDF page index 11, Ethical Considerations
exact_locators.supported_metadata: The authors report informing participants about study purpose/role/rights, obtaining verbal consent with withdrawal rights, pseudonymity/confidentiality, express permission for sensitive cultural information, and consultation with community leaders/elders.
exact_locators.restriction: This does not establish MLHKP secondary-use consent, participant permission for redistribution, or community-wide cultural validation.

rights_access_consent.decision: Promote bibliographic, methods and study-reported ethics metadata with exact locators only. Keep participant-derived cultural assertions, quotations, ritual knowledge and pseudonym-linked data gated.

evidence_promotion.reason: The accessible source permits exact-locator provenance for source/method/ethics characterization, but participant-derived cultural content requires a stricter secondary-use and cultural-access review.
